title: Pre-build demand & distribution toolkit for vibe-coded indie SaaS
one_liner: Help solo founders validate buyers and pick a distribution wedge before shipping another short-lived feature dump that dies in ~1.5 years.

target_personas.name: Vibe-coding indie founder about to launch
quotes: A lot of products are being vibe coded, released, and soon after that abandoned.
Distribution and marketing have become much more important than before - within the context that everyone can build "features" for free.

target_personas.name: OSS-first SaaS founder stuck on linear adoption
quotes: We've been trying to grow the project for months, and it's lowkey growing in stars and adoption. But it's linear.
I hate to spam in places like hn or other forums, but what strategies have you found working?

existing_solutions.name: Generic indie GTM courses / Twitter gurus / Launch checklists
weaknesses: Advice is generic and not tied to the founder's actual ICP evidence
No continuous measurement of whether demand exists before build
Optimizes for launches/spam rather than retained buyers

existing_solutions.name: Product Hunt / HN Show / launch-day bursts
weaknesses: One-day spikes without retention; OP already distrusts spam launches
Does not prevent building the wrong product first
OSS founder notes viral jumps are rare and hard to repeat

existing_solutions.name: Full marketing suites (HubSpot, Mailchimp, SEO agencies)
weaknesses: Overkill and expensive for pre-PMF solo founders
Assume you already have a product and list
Do not answer 'should I even build this?'

product_hypothesis: MVP in 4–6 weeks: a guided pre-build kit that forces ICP interviews, waitlist smoke tests, channel experiments, and a kill/continue score before more vibe-coding. Pair with a lightweight distribution playbook for OSS-first SaaS (non-spam HN/X sequencing, adopter interviews, star→user conversion). Differentiator vs courses: instrumented experiments + decision score, not content. Monetize $19–$49/mo or $99 one-shot for indie founders; later B2B cohort.
research_notes: Anchored on highest ICE item this HN-only run (product lifespan collapse, ICE 336) plus related Ask HN on growing OSS projects (ICE 210). Agent-memory theme that topped pipe_2026-10-29_001 dropped out of this week's top50; Top theme therefore shifts to indie distribution/GTM. Evidence remains HN-only—treat as directional. Prefill switching_willingness=1 is a heuristic miss: posts explicitly say features became free and marketing/distribution is the bottleneck, and OSS founder is actively seeking non-spam growth tactics. Competition is crowded content/agencies; wedge must be instrumented validation not more advice. Next: interview 12 founders who shipped a vibe-coded MVP in 2026; measure whether they would pay for a kill-score before next build. Avoid build+high until a second source (Reddit/IndieHackers) confirms WTP.

confidence_basis.rationale: Two HN posts in one month (graveyard lifespan + OSS growth ask) describe distribution as the bottleneck after vibe-coding made building cheap. Same lifespan thread also appeared in the prior HN sample but was not Top then; this week it is the strongest ICE cluster after agent-memory posts left the set. Still single-source (HN), so confidence stays medium.

evidence_ledger.claim: Indie SaaS product lifespan is collapsing as vibe-coding makes shipping features cheap while distribution fails.

evidence.quote: A lot of products are being vibe coded, released, and soon after that abandoned. It's become too cheap to produce software.
Distribution and marketing have become much more important than before - within the context that everyone can build "features" for free.

assumptions: Median lifespan drop on SaaSHub generalizes beyond that directory's selection bias.

evidence_ledger.claim: OSS-first founders already shipping still struggle to convert linear stars into non-spammy adoption jumps.

evidence.quote: We've been trying to grow the project for months, and it's lowkey growing in stars and adoption. But it's linear.
I hate to spam in places like hn or other forums, but what strategies have you found working? Specially in the realm of AI.

assumptions: Founders will pay for structured experiments rather than free HN comment advice.

unsupported_assumptions: Solo founders will pay for another validation toolkit instead of consuming free Twitter/HN advice.
An instrumented kill-score changes build behavior more than guilt/FOMO does.
OSS star growth tactics generalize into a retainable SaaS workflow.

validation_required.experiment: Interview 12 founders who shipped a vibe-coded MVP in 2026 and saw weak distribution.
validation_required.success_criterion: ≥8 admit they would have paused build if a credible kill-score existed; ≥5 name a budget ≥$20/mo or ≥$99 one-shot.

validation_required.experiment: Concierge MVP: run 5 paid ($99) 2-week demand sprints (ICP calls + waitlist + one channel test) without building product UI.
validation_required.success_criterion: ≥3 of 5 say the kill/continue memo changed their next sprint; ≥2 refer another founder.

validation_required.experiment: Landing-page smoke test: 'Don't vibe-code into the graveyard' waitlist with $29/mo intent checkbox.
validation_required.success_criterion: ≥80 emails or ≥12 paid-intent checks in 2 weeks from HN/IndieHackers alone.

switching_cost.rationale: Switching from 'just ship features' to a validation ritual has low data migration; main cost is sunk vibe-coding ego/time and learning a new weekly habit.

current_workarounds: Ship first, ask HN/X for growth tips later
Buy indie marketing courses / follow GTM influencers
One-shot Product Hunt / Show HN launches
Hire freelancers for SEO/content without ICP proof
workaround_analysis.rationale: Workarounds are abundant but OP evidence shows products still die fast; OSS founder still stuck on linear growth and rejects spam. Advice market is crowded; quality uneven and unmeasured.

buyer_mapping.user: Solo indie founder / OSS-first SaaS builder
buyer_mapping.buyer: Founder on personal card or tiny bootstrap budget
buyer_mapping.champion: Founder who already felt a failed or flat launch

persistence.rationale: As long as AI keeps collapsing build cost, distribution remains the scarce factor; not a one-off platform bug. Structural for the indie SaaS market, though advice competitors are plentiful.

economic_impact.quantification_notes: Primary loss is months of build+hosting with near-zero revenue when products die at ~1.5y median; secondary is founder burnout. Killing bad ideas early saves more cash than another feature sprint.

opportunity_score.formula: Pain × Frequency × ROI × SwitchingWill × Buyer × Persistence ÷ Competition ÷ WorkaroundQuality
